title: What If Earth Had a Dent in Its Magnetic Shield?

scenes.text: What if Earth's magnetic shield had a dent in it? It does, and it is moving.
It is called the South Atlantic Anomaly, a weak spot stretching between South America and Africa.
There, charged particles from the Sun dip closer to Earth than they should.
Satellites crossing it can glitch, so operators switch off sensitive instruments on purpose.
The International Space Station, about 350 kilometers up, gets blips in its instruments each time it passes through.
Satellite data shows it drifting west and may be splitting in two. Its cause is liquid iron 1,800 miles down.

description:
What if Earth's magnetic field had a weak spot?
The South Atlantic Anomaly lets more solar particles reach orbit, so satellites switch off instruments as they cross it.
What should we run through next?
